title: Queen's Indian Defense: Fianchetto Variation
line: Both bishops face each other on the long diagonal, and the fight is for a center square on it.

steps.text: The Queen's Indian, and White gets ready to put its own bishop on the long diagonal.
Put your bishop on the long diagonal too. The two bishops face each other.

also.c8a6: That is the most played line, against the pawn on c4. This lesson goes on with the long diagonal.

steps.text: Bring out the other bishop, to get ready to castle.
Castle, to get your king to safety.
steps.after: White's knight comes out to help a pawn to e4.

steps.text: Jump into e4 yourself, the square your bishop watches. The knight offers a trade.
Trade knights. White has one piece less to fight for e4.
Push the pawn on c7 two squares, at White's center.
Move the pawn in front of your queen one square. It keeps White's pieces off e5.
steps.after: Black is solid, and its bishop still rules the long diagonal.

summary: The bishops face each other on the long diagonal. Black jumps into the center with a knight and trades it off.
